A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. The main text, equations, algorithms, Tables 1–2, Figures 1–2 and Appendices A–F are available and support reliable comparison despite the changed typesetting.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic linear-regression experiments in Figure 1 and California Housing experiments in Appendix F, Figure 2.

after.justification: v2 retains the original synthetic regression and California Housing experimental results in Figures 1–2 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same minimizer approximation, Gaussian output perturbation and trimmed-mean robust training. Their inputs, update rules, approximation thresholds and noise scales are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic linear regression under in-distribution and shifted-label out-of-distribution conditions, plus California Housing regression. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 1a retains Algorithm 1 versus DP-SGD; Figure 1b and Figure 2 retain Algorithm 1 versus Algorithm 2. The added citation near Definition 1 does not introduce an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix F retains 10,000 synthetic in-distribution samples with 20 deletions, 1,000 out-of-distribution samples and a label offset of 10^3. Metrics, forget fractions, unlearning budgets and optimizer settings also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The dimension sweep in Figure 1a and the out-of-distribution convergence comparisons across forget-set sizes in Figures 1b and 2 are retained. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: The experimental text, captions and Appendix F retain the same statistical reporting. No repeated-run counts, seed details, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures are added, removed or revised.

E6.justification: Figures 1–2 reproduce the same plotted results and findings, including the reported possibility of 10-fold slower unlearning with non-robust Algorithm 1. Numerical captions and the entries in Tables 1–2 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions, propositions, theorems, Corollary 2 and supporting lemmas retain their assumptions and mathematical statements. Appendices A–E preserve the corresponding derivations, counterexample and proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims: dimension-independent in-distribution deletion capacity, potentially severe out-of-distribution slowdown and robust training that enables efficient certified unlearning.

C2.justification: Both versions give the same interpolation-error explanation for robust training, qualifications concerning Lipschitz assumptions and interpretation of empirical slowdowns. The open directions concerning unified bounds and more complex models are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Remark 6 and Appendix F retain the same iteration-bound guidance, Opacus implementation reference, synthetic-data generation, learning-rate guidance and empirical strong-convexity estimation. No implementation or code/data access information is added.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Neel et al. (2021) alongside Ginart et al. (2019) and Sekhari et al. (2021) when attributing prior approximate-unlearning definitions. This modestly expands attribution; Neel et al. was already cited elsewhere, and the broader positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Front-matter and copy edits include the abbreviated EPFL affiliation, added author emails, shortened visiting-work footnote and corrected Łojasiewicz spelling. Sections 1–6 and Appendices A–F retain their order and essentially the same prose.

P2.justification: The entire document is reset in the ICLR conference format, changing body and heading typography, text width, spacing and running headers. Tables and plots are resized, while algorithms, figures and surrounding text are repositioned throughout the main paper and appendices. Their underlying content is retained.

improvement.justification: Both versions provide the same algorithms, theoretical guarantees, proofs, empirical evidence and reproducibility information. The added citation slightly improves attribution, but the remaining changes are conference formatting and minor copy edits. These do not produce a meaningful overall quality difference.
